mechanism.name: Logistic projection under an even nonlinear Gaussian-mixture response
generation_equations: B is equiprobable on {-1,+1}; G~N_4(0,Sigma), Sigma_jk=0.8^abs(j-k), independently. X=B*1+G.
Y|X~Bernoulli(expit(sum_{j=1}^4 [0.9*X_j^4*sin(X_j)^6-2*X_j^2+2.2])). Conditional draws are independent across rows.

Two independent samples from the same population: source_n_labeled rows with observed Y and source_n_unlabeled rows with observed X only. R=1 in the first labeled block; Y_obs=Y there. R=0 in the remaining block; Y_obs=0 is a placeholder.

sampling.dependence: Independent rows, with within-row dependence specified by the equations.
sampling.predictor_provenance: The generator exposes covariates as auxiliary information; fitted predictions are supplied by subsequent statistical methods using permitted labeled data and their documented training or cross-fitting splits. This contribution supplies the sampling law and observed data; later methods specify training and validation partitions. Prediction columns are absent.

assumptions: Independent sampling units; labeled and unlabeled samples are independent draws from the same joint/marginal population.
Label availability is fixed by sampling design independently of generated values, corresponding to MCAR sampling.
The stated distributions, independence conditions and selected population functional define the target. Its numerical verification applies to the declared scenario.

properties.notes: All four coordinates affect the nonlinear response probability even though the linear logistic projection slopes vanish by symmetry. effective_dimension counts the generating response support. The Gaussian mixture is correlated; Bernoulli conditional variance varies with X. effective_dimension counts inputs that determine the conditional response law, including an observed surrogate or the sole tail-dependent auxiliary variable; correlated extra coordinates may carry additional information. high_dimensional compares total dimension with source labeled sample size. Interactions marks a nonadditive response/probability map.

estimand.name: theta_logistic[1]
estimand.definition: First slope in the population logistic-loss projection of Y on (1,X1,...,X4).

truth.expression: First slope in the population logistic-loss projection of Y on (1,X1,...,X4).
truth.derivation: The distribution of X is centrally symmetric and its response probability q satisfies q(-X)=q(X). Hence E[X]=E[X*q(X)]=0. At zero slopes and intercept logit(E[q(X)]), every population score vanishes. Full support makes the logistic risk strictly convex, so all projection slopes are exactly zero.

adaptations: Select S2 with p=4,n=250,N=1000 from Figure 12(b).
Return the first slope of the source population logistic projection; its zero truth follows from central symmetry.
Represent independent labeled/unlabeled samples in a single table: all X columns, label indicator R and Y_obs. A zero on an R=0 row is a finite placeholder.
The generate argument n counts total rows. Source total yields exact source allocation; other n use nearest-integer ratio allocation with both groups nonempty.
Use local PCG64 random streams, with independent covariate and response-noise streams. Each row remains an independent population draw.
